title: Google launches Deep Review AI tool to help researchers catch manuscript errors
key_facts: Google Research released Deep Review on 14 Oct 2026 to flag mathematical errors, logical gaps and unsupported claims in technical documents.
It grew out of the Paper Assistant Tool, piloted at STOC, ICML, NeurIPS and ICLR, which gave feedback on more than 15,000 manuscripts.
Deep Review splits documents into sections, uses AI agents to examine them and Google Search to check for hallucinations.
A review takes about 10 to 20 minutes.
In a June preprint the earlier tool found 89.7 percent of known errors in a benchmark subset versus 55.2 percent for one Gemini 3.1 Pro response (29 errors, 26 papers).
Pilot users reported cases where it wrongly challenged proofs.
Google offers two free reviews per week; uploaded documents are not used for training and kept for one year.
quote_evidence: The public launch follows pilots that provided feedback on more than 15,000 manuscripts, according to Google.
Pilot participants also reported cases in which the system incorrectly challenged proofs or arguments
why_it_matters_hint: Aims to ease the verification bottleneck as AI makes polished papers cheap to produce.
notes: Performance figures are Google's own and from a small benchmark.
